approvalText: I approve ME-12 citation verification — all 5 sources, exactly as implemented.

rows.title: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension: a review of risk factors, management and current challenges
rows.citation: Cannon JE, Jenkins DP, Hoole SP. Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension: a review of risk factors, management and current challenges. Expert Rev Cardiovasc Ther. 2022;20(1):35-43. PMID 35081846. doi:10.1080/14779072.2022.2034499.
rows.publicationGuard: Restrict the broad pulmonary-hypertension target to separately established chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension after a documented pulmonary embolism. Require persistent mismatched perfusion or chronic thromboembolic/fibrotic obstruction after an appropriate post-PE anticoagulation interval and hemodynamically confirmed pulmonary hypertension under accepted criteria. Do not infer CTEPH from acute PE, persistent dyspnea, hypoxemia, or an echocardiographic estimate alone. Preserve left-heart disease, other lung disease or hypoxia, chronic thromboembolic disease without pulmonary hypertension, drugs/toxins, and other pulmonary-hypertension etiologies as competing explanations.

rows.title: A systematic review of epileptic seizures in adults with subdural haematomas
rows.citation: Won SY, Konczalla J, Dubinski D, et al. A systematic review of epileptic seizures in adults with subdural haematomas. Seizure. 2017;45:28-35. PMID 27914224. doi:10.1016/j.seizure.2016.11.017.
rows.publicationGuard: Require objectively documented subdural hematoma and separately established epileptic seizures or a seizure disorder with compatible chronology. Do not infer a chronic seizure disorder from prophylactic antiseizure medication, transient altered mental status, or an unconfirmed spell. Distinguish an isolated acute symptomatic seizure from recurrent unprovoked seizures or epilepsy when the target diagnosis requires that distinction. Preserve pre-existing epilepsy, additional traumatic brain injury, stroke, infection, metabolic or toxic disturbance, medication or substance effects, and other seizure etiologies.

rows.title: Optic Neuritis in Multiple Sclerosis-A Review of Molecular Mechanisms Involved in the Degenerative Process
rows.citation: Ciapa MA, Salaru DL, Statescu C, Sascau RA, Bogdanici CM. Optic Neuritis in Multiple Sclerosis-A Review of Molecular Mechanisms Involved in the Degenerative Process. Curr Issues Mol Biol. 2022;44(9):3959-3979. PMID 36135184. doi:10.3390/cimb44090272.
rows.publicationGuard: Require established multiple sclerosis and a separately diagnosed optic-neuritis phenotype compatible with inflammatory demyelinating optic neuropathy. Do not infer optic neuritis from nonspecific visual loss, eye pain, abnormal imaging, or multiple-sclerosis diagnosis alone. Preserve neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, MOG-antibody disease, ischemic, infectious, compressive, toxic/nutritional, hereditary, and other optic-neuropathy causes.

rows.title: Predictors of Hypothyroidism in Hodgkin Lymphoma Survivors After Intensity Modulated Versus 3-Dimensional Radiation Therapy
rows.citation: Pinnix CC, Cella L, Andraos TY, et al. Predictors of Hypothyroidism in Hodgkin Lymphoma Survivors After Intensity Modulated Versus 3-Dimensional Radiation Therapy. Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys. 2018;101(3):530-540. PMID 29681481. doi:10.1016/j.ijrobp.2018.03.003.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented Hodgkin lymphoma, documented thyroid-exposing neck or supradiaphragmatic radiation treatment consistent with the source phenotype, and separately established hypothyroidism after treatment with compatible chronology. Do not infer hypothyroidism from Hodgkin lymphoma or chemotherapy alone. Preserve autoimmune thyroid disease, thyroid surgery or radioiodine, medications, pituitary or hypothalamic disease, congenital thyroid disease, and other causes of hypothyroidism.

rows.title: Reactive arthritis: a clinical review
rows.citation: Jubber A, Moorthy A. Reactive arthritis: a clinical review. J R Coll Physicians Edinb. 2021;51(3):288-297. PMID 34528623. doi:10.4997/JRCPE.2021.319.
rows.publicationGuard: Require established reactive arthritis and separately documented anterior uveitis by appropriate ophthalmic evaluation. Do not infer uveitis from reactive arthritis, conjunctivitis, red eye, ocular irritation, or photophobia alone. Preserve infectious uveitis, HLA-B27-associated uveitis from another spondyloarthritis, sarcoidosis, inflammatory bowel disease, medication-related disease, trauma, and other ocular inflammatory causes.
